newsitem.title: UK: Bell Cablemedia year revenues rise.
newsitem.headline: Bell Cablemedia year revenues rise.

text.p: Britain's Bell Cablemedia Plc said on Tuesday total revenues rose 78 percent to 76.9 million stg in 1996, including its controlling stake in Videotron Holdings Plc.
Excluding Videotron, revenues rose 69 percent to 73.2 million stg compared to the year-ago period, the company said.
Net loss for the year was 95.7 million stg, or 1.52 stg per American Depositary Share, compared to a loss of 47.4 million stg, or 0.76 stg, in the year-ago period.

The increase in the net loss was due partly to higher depreciation and amortization in 1996, while the year-earlier results included a gain of 9.0 million stg from the initial public offering of Videotron shares.

Bell Cablemedia raised its stake in Videotron to about 82 percent last year as part of the proposed merger of the two companies with Cable and Wireless Plc's Mercury unit and NYNEX CableComms, part of NYNEX Corp.

Bell Cablemedia said customer churn rates, excluding Videotron, fell to 24.2 percent in 1996 from 27.3 percent for cable television, while residential telephony churn rose to 18.3 percent from 17.3 percent.
The company said it passed 87,199 homes in the fourth quarter -- more than in any other quarter of 1996 -- bringing the total homes passed in the year to 244,544.
Capital expenditure, excluding Videotron, was 200.6 million stg compared with 182.6 million stg in 1995.
